learning.title: A lock-race test asserts after the race returns, and checks 500s and pg_locks, not only assertNoDeadlock
learning.trigger: A test races two ticket operations with holdRow and raceInOrder to prove a lock order, or to prove that a lock is taken before an insert.
learning.mistake: An assertion thrown inside a racer left the holdRow hold open, so fixture teardown waited on it and the run hung instead of failing. assertNoDeadlock on a fulfilled Response passes when Postgres killed one side as a deadlock victim, because the victim answers an HTTP 500. A missing lock whose later insert takes a key-share on the same row through a foreign key cannot cause a deadlock at all, so a race never shows it missing.
learning.rule: Record observations inside the racer and assert after raceInOrder returns. For HTTP operations install the problem-error reporter for the race and assert it saw no 5xx. To pin a lock that a foreign key would otherwise hide, read pg_locks of the session queued behind the hold and assert it holds no non-AccessShare lock on the later tables, then pair that with assertNoDeadlock.

verification.requirement: Removing the lock, or taking the task row before the ticket row, fails the case with a deadlock or a lock assertion, not a hang.
